summary.headline: M&M Financial Q2 FY27 PAT rose 55% YoY to INR 882 crore, with GS2+GS3 at 8.1% and credit cost at 1.6%.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as steady across growth, margin and risk, with disbursements up 22% YoY and AUM up 15% YoY. Asset quality improved, with GS2+GS3 at 8.1% (near all-time lows) and inter-quarter volatility reduced; credit cost was 1.6% against a 1.3-1.7% guided range. ROA was about 2.2% in the quarter (H1 about 2.3%), dented by excess liquidity buffers and high trade advances, while cost of funds is expected to rise after one 25 bps repo hike with more hikes priced in. Management said it sees no change to its FY31 targets of 16-18% AUM growth, 1.3-1.7% credit cost and 2.2-2.5% ROA.

guidance_outlook: Long-term AUM growth target maintained at 16-18%; management declined to give quarterly or yearly guidance.
Credit cost guided within 1.3-1.7%; no near-term challenge seen and no additional overlay planned at present.
Cost of funds expected to trend upward: a 25 bps hike affects about 10 bps of existing stock within a quarter via floating resets, and refinancing adds further cost.

NIM expected to be challenging; management said it is at the lower end of the 7%+ range needed for 2.2-2.5% ROA. Loan income expected to recover as trade advances and excess liquidity convert into earning assets.
Mahindra Rural Housing Finance merger: appointed date 1 April 2027, effective date targeted June-July 2027, pending NCLT and some regulatory approvals.
capex_capacity: Liquidity buffer roughly doubled YoY in rupee terms; management said it could be reduced somewhat if the environment eases.
Mortgage plan: MRHFL has 400 branches and MMFSL 1,400; the HFC is being folded into the parent, with plans for affordable housing, LAP and some prime housing (prime housing started in August).
Headcount rising after two static years to support wheels, SME and mortgage growth; off-roll to on-roll migration program in place.
AI toolkits: 75% of back office covered by enabled workflows; 12 regional AI vernacular bots in call centres. Roughly 10% of disbursements are AI-led, per the question from an analyst.
demand_pricing: Navratri first 10 days: underlying commerce and unit disbursements down YoY, with tractors seeing a somewhat sharper decline; last year's base was inflated by pre-GST-cut demand.
VAHAN registration data showed rural and semi-urban vehicle growth marginally above urban and metro through September.
Pricing: competition is intense in salaried segments (not served). Self-employed agri segments have less competition, leaving room to price incremental wheels loans higher; no broad repricing yet.
Trade advances deliberately raised above normal levels ahead of festive season growth.

Insurance: a draft consultation paper may cut fee income from motor insurance (MIBL) and corporate agency; fee income had risen from 1% to 1.6% of assets, partly from insurance. Quantification deferred until the final regulation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-of-funds trajectory for FY27 given the rate hike and liquidity holdings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects cost of funds to rise after one 25 bps hike and more priced in; a 25 bps move resets about 10 bps of floating stock within a quarter. Refinancing is at higher rates. Some liquidity buffer flexibility exists but not large.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost trajectory after a flat H1 with no seasonality: could it drop below 1.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 1.3-1.7%, citing existing stock keeping H2 GS3 stable and rural cash flows improving in Q3-Q4. The INR 852 crore overlay is adequate and no further buffer is planned now.

qa_highlights.question: Is the trade advance increase in others (8.2% of AUM) driving growth visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, trade advances were deployed at a clear level above normal to support Q3 festive growth. Personal loans to existing customers are also building; prime housing started in August and will be disclosed separately later.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on tractor collections in drought-affected states such as Maharashtra?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to call: tractor half-yearly instalments fall due at end of rabi/kharif and collections are not yet at that point. Teams are assessing stress case by case; management does not plan to change its tractor stance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the housing finance merger and mortgage push change returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage is an early drag on ROA but seen as strategic; management noted the HFC-NBFC cost-of-funds arbitrage is narrowing and cited the merger rationale of simplifying duplicated functions.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM fall below 7% in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM expansion will be hard; loan income should recover as trade advances and excess liquidity convert, and fee income has some headroom. Half-year loan income reflects the run-rate better than Q2 alone.

risks_watch: Drought in 3 states and 282 drought-prone districts could raise tractor stress, especially after the half-yearly collection cycle.
Further repo hikes and refinancing at higher rates may compress NIM before loan repricing (fixed-rate vehicle book).
The draft insurance consultation paper could reduce fee income from MIBL and corporate agency.
Navratri demand softness versus a high base; H2 disbursement growth is uncertain against last year's strong H2.
Liquidity buffer and trade advances are drags on ROA until they convert into earning assets.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and operating metrics, but cautious on near-term cost of funds, NIM, festive demand and insurance regulation. Management was evasive on disclosing book maturity and segment-level details, and declined quarterly or yearly guidance.

So, we are a franchise that wants to grow in the high teens as we say.
The PAT growth is not, is not sustainable at the 70% levels.
We will not chase any growth at the cost of either price or risk.
